title: 1p a Day Becomes £667.95… Why Most People Quit in December 😱 #shorts
description:
Save 1p on day 1, 2p on day 2 … £3.65 on day 365, and you'll have £667.95 by New Year's Eve.

The maths: 1p + 2p + … + 365p = 365 × 366 ÷ 2 = 66,795p = £667.95.

The catch: December alone costs £108.50, right before Christmas.
The fix most people miss: do it backwards. Start at £3.65 on 1 January and December costs just £4.96. Same total, and your savings earn interest for longer.

Level up: repeat it for 10 years, invested at an assumed 7% a year, and it could grow to about £9,230 (£6,680 paid in).

Your turn: in a leap year, what's the total? Comment your answer 👇
📩 Send this to the friend who says pennies don't matter.

Illustration only. 365-day year (2027). Assumes 7% a year after fees, with each year's £667.95 invested at the end of the year. Investments can fall as well as rise and you may get back less than you put in. General education, not financial advice.

Music and sound effects: original, made for this channel.

assumptions: 365 days (2027 is not a leap year): 1p on day 1 rising by 1p a day to 365p on day 365
£667.95 invested at the end of each year for 10 years at 7% a year after fees = £9,228.70 (paid in £6,679.50)
Leap year (comment-question answer, not shown): 366 x 367 / 2 = 67,161p = £671.61
